source.title: Noisy Concurrent Training for Efficient Learning under Label Noise
source.authors: Fahad Sarfraz; E. Arani; Bahram Zonooz

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests fitting random labels with a different setup: frozen learned representations plus a newly added MLP, rather than end-to-end training of the original networks.
record.gate_note: The paper measures how well frozen representations plus an added MLP fit random binary labels. It does not report results for shuffled pixels, label-noise sweeps of the kind in V4, or the other versions. Results cited from prior work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: Figure 1 reports the study's own training-loss and accuracy trajectories for clean and noisy training subsets, bearing on V6. The standard cross-entropy comparator shows later memorization of noisy labels. The frozen-representation probe in Figure 3 measures information compression and does not test V1's unchanged, end-to-end training setup.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the Section 5.2 compression interpretation, but omits the paper's main conclusion: NCT improves robustness to label noise through collaborative learning, dynamic balancing, and target variability, offering an alternative to filtering or down-weighting noisy examples.
record.recipe_differences: Uses frozen learned representations with a newly added 2-layer MLP to fit random binary labels; this differs from training the original network end to end on randomly labeled images.
record.method_sensitivity: The study compares clean, symmetric-20%, and symmetric-50% label-noise training conditions; it reports that NCT consistently learns more compressed features than standard training.

fits_no_version.finding: NCT's frozen representations fit random binary labels less well than standard-training representations, which the authors interpret as stronger information compression.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random-label probe accuracy on frozen representations can distinguish representations learned by NCT and standard training.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Workshop/Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV 2021)
record.problems: The random-label evaluation uses frozen representations and an added MLP rather than end-to-end network training. Figure 3 is the only location for the measured accuracies, and the supplied text does not provide their numerical values. The paper reports a mean and standard deviation of three seeds for its broader experiments, but does not state uncertainty for Figure 3.
record.rows_left_out: None. Figure 3 results are retained as separate figure-only rows for each model and label-noise condition.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error on completely random labels using the unchanged end-to-end architecture and hyperparameters, with chance test performance.
Training-time comparison between true and random labels, and convergence slowing across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit throughout a corruption sweep from zero to complete corruption, with test error rising steadily toward chance.
Whether weight decay, dropout, and augmentation prevent fitting completely random labels, and generalization after removing these regularizers.
Completely random-label datasets and generality beyond the illustrated CIFAR-10 setting; numerical learning-onset differences are not recoverable from the supplied trajectories.

missing.what: The study's own clean-versus-noisy training loss and accuracy trajectories for standard CE, showing later noisy-label memorization. Add rows capturing the temporal comparison underlying the V6 verdict; retain qualitative evidence where curve values cannot be read.
missing.locator: Figure 1 and accompanying discussion in Sections 1, 3.3, and 3.4

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V1 limits_scope verdict: the compression probe does not establish a qualification of V1. Figure 3's caption says lower training error means stronger compression, contradicting Section 5.2, which says lower training accuracy; the authors' stated comparison follows the latter interpretation. NCT's deliberately designed suppression of memorization does not independently challenge V6.

versions.untested_parts: Tests fitting random binary labels only after freezing representations and adding a 2-layer MLP. Does not test end-to-end fitting of completely random training labels by the original networks, test error at chance, unchanged training hyperparameters, or generalization on true labels.

rows.subject: standard training (CE)
rows.operation_detail: Fit random binary labels using a 2-layer MLP added to frozen learned representations.
rows.measure: Training accuracy when fitting random binary labels; lower training accuracy is described as indicating better information compression.
rows.note: The text describes the comparison as a study of how well frozen representations fit random labels but gives no numerical result outside the figure.
rows.check: Frozen representations with an added MLP measure a compression proxy, not V1. Figure 3 contains numerical accuracy annotations in the supplied text, so 'figure only' overstates their absence; their assignment to individual bars is not reliably preserved.

relationships.reason: Based on Figure 1 and its accompanying text, rather than the extracted rows: clean/noisy training trajectories illustrate initial pattern learning followed by later noisy-label memorization. Exact trajectory values are unavailable.
relationships.display_finding: Clean and noisy training trajectories showed initial pattern learning followed by later noisy-label memorization.

reader_labels.condition: Frozen CIFAR-10 representations with an added MLP, across clean and symmetric-noise training settings
reader_labels.reason: NCT fits the random-label probe less well than standard training, according to the authors’ description of greater information compression (R2, R4, R6); the probe does not establish whether the original end-to-end networks fit random labels.
